metadata.title: Logix / AION technical catalog for the alternative-history story
metadata.purpose: Canonical structured technical/product catalog separated from the narrative story document.

included: Logix/AION technologies and standards used in products
peripherals, expansion devices, and separately/bundled devices
Logix/AION and explicitly offered third-party software
support, training, developer, certification, and licensing services
post-document technical additions explicitly stated by the user in this chat
excluded: competitor products except where a Logix device directly interfaces with them
Adam's secret CAD/lithography facility because it is internal production tooling rather than a product/component sold or bundled to customers
technical features invented in assistant analysis but not explicitly stated by the user

source_conventions.uploaded_story: Specification explicitly present in the uploaded story document.
source_conventions.conversation_addition: Specification added explicitly by the user later in this conversation and not yet present in the uploaded document.
source_conventions.derived_relationship: A structural relationship inferred only to avoid duplication, such as Aurelia+ inheriting unchanged Aurelia features. No new technical capability is added by the inference.

schema_notes.introduced: Every catalog object uses an introduced object with event_name and event_start_date. Partial dates use YYYY-MM and include date_precision=month. For third-party base parts, the date means first use in a Logix/AION product in this scenario, not the vendor’s historical market introduction.
schema_notes.technologies: Technology specifications describe reusable standards/architectures, not per-product implementation counts. Product-specific port/slot/count details belong to computers/devices/base_parts.
schema_notes.computers: Each computer is fully specified. No inheritance/override mechanism is used.
schema_notes.bundles: Commercial packaging is represented separately in root-level offered_bundles.
schema_notes.references: Cross-references use stable IDs such as technology.flexibus, part.z80b and device.flexibus_keyboard.

specification.attachment_model: dynamic attachment is supported when the bus is inactive
specification.openness: The technical specification is published for third-party implementation.
specification.compatibility_policy: Logix commits to forward peripheral compatibility across future Logix computer generations.

specification.driver_storage: expansion device carries its driver/identification code in ROM
specification.design_goal: automatic identification and execution without manual switch configuration
specification.forward_design_policy: connector/pin standards may reserve unused capacity for later generations

specification.execution_model: system and application components may execute directly from ROM where practical
specification.distribution_model: replaceable ROM/EEPROM cartridges are used for system and application distribution
specification.upgrade_model: software/firmware can be upgraded by replacing the relevant cartridge
specification.design_goal: reduce RAM consumption and provide controlled, replaceable system images

specification.monitor_palette_control: Color/greyscale registers may be changed using Control commands during vertical retrace.

specification.design_goal: common network protocol stack across Aurelia CP/M and Artemis/AIONix clients and servers
specification.interoperability_model: IP is kept above the Logix-specific physical/data-link layer so future faster link technologies can preserve higher-level software.

introduced.event_name: NCC 1981 — Logix networking / Artemis PRO launch

specification.topology: active star through a multiport hub/repeater/arbiter
specification.signaling: balanced differential serial signaling compatible in principle with EIA-422-class line drivers/receivers

pair_assignment.pair_4: reserved for diagnostics or later expansion

specification.media_access: hub-controlled polling/grant; one station is granted transmit access at a time, avoiding collision-detection hardware
specification.framing: HDLC-inspired bit-oriented framing with address/control fields and 16-bit frame check sequence
specification.hub_behavior: receives an admitted frame and repeats it to the other active ports; adapters filter by destination address
specification.station_addressing: locally assigned link address stored/configured by the adapter; broadcast supported
specification.design_goal: simple, deterministic and inexpensive LAN implementation using technology comfortably available by 1981

research_basis.fact: Balanced-voltage digital interface standard existed by 1975.
HDLC elements of procedure were standardized by 1979.
Modular telephone connectors were established in the 1970s; 8-position variants are historically plausible hardware.

source.note: Proposed to close the previously open link-layer specification while staying conservative for 1981.
